title: The Radio Man (የሬዲዮ ሰው)
logline: My father taught himself to repair radios in a small Ethiopian town, and that is why I write code today.
audience: My family (parents, siblings, cousins at home and in the diaspora) and young Ethiopians learning tech; watching on phones, mostly vertical, shared on WhatsApp and Telegram.
intent: Feel pride in an ordinary man's curiosity, and see that fixing radios and writing code are the same gift passed from father to child.

style.style_block: warm hand-painted illustration, soft painterly brushwork, gentle film grain, 1980s small Ethiopian town, muted palette of ochre, warm brown, faded teal and cream, soft window light, subject centred in frame, nostalgic and intimate

characters.name: Father, in his early twenties (1980s)
characters.description: a young Ethiopian man in his early twenties, slim, short curly black hair, thin moustache, warm brown skin, white short-sleeved button shirt, brown trousers

characters.name: Father, today

voice.style_instruction: Read slowly and warmly, like telling a story to a grandchild at bedtime.

lines: Images: FLUX.2 klein | Voice: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS | Music: ACE-Step 1.5
My father's story, shared with his consent

shots.reason: Establish the town at dawn before we meet anyone.
shots.image_prompt: a small hillside town at dawn, tin roofs and eucalyptus trees, mist in the valley
shots.motion_prompt: mist drifts slowly across the valley, the camera pushes in very gently
shots.narration: Every Saturday, before the sun was fully up, my grandmother walked to the market.
shots.subtitle_en: Every Saturday, before the sun was fully up, my grandmother walked to the market.

shots.reason: Introduce her, so the viewer knows whose story this is.
shots.image_prompt: standing in the doorway of a mud-brick house, holding a woven basket
shots.motion_prompt: she adjusts her shawl, the camera is fixed
shots.narration: She wrapped her shawl twice, picked up her basket, and called my name.
shots.subtitle_en: She wrapped her shawl twice, picked up her basket, and called my name.

shots.reason: The child's hand in hers: the relationship in one image.
shots.image_prompt: close-up of an old woman's hand holding a small child's hand on a dirt path
shots.narration: I held her hand the whole way.
shots.subtitle_en: I held her hand the whole way.

shots.reason: The walk itself: distance and effort.
shots.image_prompt: walking along a dirt road between green fields, seen from behind, small child beside her
shots.narration: The road was long, but she never hurried and she never stopped.
shots.subtitle_en: The road was long, but she never hurried and she never stopped.

shots.reason: Arrival: the market's colour and life.
shots.image_prompt: a busy open-air market, piles of spices and coffee beans, colourful umbrellas
shots.narration: At the market, everyone knew her.
shots.subtitle_en: At the market, everyone knew her.

shots.reason: Her character: how she treated people.
shots.image_prompt: laughing with a spice seller across a table of red berbere
shots.narration: She bargained hard, laughed louder, and always paid a little extra.
shots.subtitle_en: She bargained hard, laughed louder, and always paid a little extra.

shots.reason: The lesson she repeated, the emotional centre.
shots.image_prompt: her face in soft afternoon light, looking down kindly at someone just out of frame
shots.narration: Slowly, slowly, she would say, an egg will walk.
shots.subtitle_en: "Slowly, slowly," she would say, "an egg will walk."

shots.reason: Return to the road, now empty: time has passed.
shots.image_prompt: the same dirt road between green fields at sunset, empty, long shadows
shots.narration: I still walk that road in my mind, slowly, the way she taught me.
shots.subtitle_en: I still walk that road in my mind, slowly, the way she taught me.
